action_description: Hero is on the button with 1000 chips. Blinds 10/20. Opponent raises to 100.
explanation: You have a strong draw with a gutshot and overcards, raising is optimal.

action_description: Hero is in the big blind with 500 chips. Blinds 10/20. Opponent bets 200 into a 400 pot.
explanation: You have 7-high with no draw. Folding is the only option.

action_description: Hero is UTG with 2000 chips. Blinds 25/50. You have pocket aces.
explanation: Pocket aces pre-flop should be raised for value.

action_description: Hero is in position with 1500 chips. Blinds 15/30. Opponent c-bets 100 into 150.
explanation: With a pocket pair and overcards on board, calling in position is standard.

action_description: Hero has an open-ended straight draw with two overcards. Pot is 300, opponent bets 150.
explanation: You have a strong draw with overcards. A semi-bluff raise applies maximum pressure.

action_description: Hero has a small pocket pair. Board is dry with one overcard. Opponent bets 50 into 100.
explanation: With no set and a dry board, folding to a bet is correct.

action_description: Hero has the nut flush! Pot is 500, opponent bets 300.
explanation: You have the nuts. Raise for maximum value.

action_description: Hero has a flush draw. Pot is 200, opponent bets 100.
explanation: With a nut flush draw, calling gives you the right pot odds to continue.

action_description: Hero has a straight on a monotone board. Pot is 1000, opponent goes all-in for 500.
explanation: On a monotone board with a non-nut straight, folding to an all-in is correct.

action_description: Hero has a royal flush! Pot is 1000, opponent checks.
explanation: You have the absolute nuts. Bet or raise to extract maximum value.

action_description: Hero flopped a set of eights! Pot is 150, opponent bets 75.
explanation: You have a set on a dry board. Raise to build the pot.

action_description: Hero has pocket jacks on an AKQ board. Opponent bets 200 into 400.
explanation: Your jacks are likely beaten by the AKQ board. Folding is correct.

action_description: Hero flopped a set of deuces! Pot is 100, opponent checks.
explanation: You have a set. Bet for value.

action_description: Hero has the nut flush on a very coordinated board. Opponent bets big.
explanation: You have the nut flush. Raise for maximum value.

action_description: Hero has a straight flush! Pot is 300, opponent bets 150.
explanation: You have a straight flush. Slow-play or raise for value.

action_description: Hero has an open-ended straight draw. Pot is 250, opponent bets 125.
explanation: With a straight draw, calling gives you correct pot odds.

action_description: Hero has a king-high flush. Pot is 400, opponent bets 200.
explanation: You have a flush but not the nut flush. Calling is safer than raising.

action_description: Hero has ace-high on a very dry board. Opponent checks.
explanation: On a dry board with ace-high, checking behind is standard.

action_description: Hero has a small flush. Pot is 500, opponent bets 250.
explanation: With a small flush on a coordinated board, folding to a big bet is correct.

action_description: Hero has a flush draw and an open-ended straight draw (combo draw). Pot is 200, opponent bets 100.
explanation: With a massive combo draw, a semi-bluff raise is optimal.

action_description: Hero has a straight flush! Pot is 1000, opponent bets 500.
explanation: You have a straight flush. Raise for maximum value.

action_description: Hero has a straight flush! Pot is 500, opponent checks.
explanation: You have the nuts. Bet for value.

action_description: Hero has a gutshot straight draw. Pot is 150, opponent bets 75.
explanation: With only a gutshot, the pot odds are not sufficient. Fold.

action_description: Hero has a flush and a straight! Pot is 300, opponent bets 150.
explanation: You have a very strong hand. Raise for maximum value.

action_description: Hero has pocket kings on an ace-high board. Opponent bets 200 into 300.
explanation: With an ace on the board, your kings are likely beaten. Fold.

action_description: Hero has an open-ended straight draw and a flush draw. Pot is 400, opponent bets 200.
explanation: With a massive combo draw, a semi-bluff raise is optimal.

action_description: Hero flopped a set of threes! Pot is 200, opponent bets 100.
explanation: You have a set. Raise to build the pot and extract value.

action_description: Hero has an open-ended straight draw and a flush draw. Pot is 150, opponent bets 75.
explanation: With a massive combo draw, a semi-bluff raise is optimal.

action_description: Hero has a straight flush! Pot is 600, opponent goes all-in for 300.
explanation: You have a straight flush. Calling the all-in is correct.

action_description: Hero has a wheel straight and a flush! Pot is 500, opponent bets 250.
explanation: You have a very strong hand. Raise for maximum value.

action_description: Hero has a straight! Pot is 300, opponent bets 150.
explanation: You have a straight. Raise for value.
